h1: How to Test Ad Creatives Without Guessing
lead: To test ad creatives, change one thing at a time, make a few versions from the same photo or a product link, and run them together before you spend more. A version can include a script, an AI presenter, and a voiceover.

sections.h2: What is an AI video ad you can test?
paras: An AI video ad is a short paid clip made from your product: words for the opening, a presenter, a spoken voice, and the cut, starting from a photo, a short description, or the product page link.
The test rules do not change. One difference between files, the same audience and budget, and a result you read only after each file has actually played.

sections.h2: How do I compare ad versions from one product?
paras: Keep the photo, the length, and the shape the same, and change only how the clip starts.

For a plain round wall clock, one version can open on the face coming into focus at dawn, another on a hand hanging it on kitchen tile, and a third on the clock leaving its box. Photo ads work the same way. A mug can sit on a counter, on a desk, or as a wrapped gift, with the same mug and the same line added later. When the single change is the presenter or the tone, ask for that and leave the product still. Build the still versions with the [AI ad image generator](page:social-ad-photos).

Home brand. Example: one still becomes a clip, and the room stays the room in the photo.

sections.h2: How do I keep ad creative testing fair for a small business?
paras: Change only one thing between versions. If the opening, the setting, and the offer all move at once, you spend money and learn nothing.
Worth testing, one at a time: the opening moment, the setting, the shape, the length, and the line you add afterward. Start with the opening. It decides whether anyone sees the rest.
sections.alt: Adult hands place the same plain round wall clock beside blank color cards.

sections.h2: How should the versions run side by side?
paras: Put them in one campaign with the same audience, the same budget, and the same product page.

Many ad accounts let several ads share one group. Some also offer a built-in test that shows each version to part of the audience. The account may push spend toward one version early. A version that barely ran has not been tested. Do not edit the ads while the test is live. A change can reset delivery and blur the result.
sections.alt: Adult hands hold the same plain round wall clock in two matched side-by-side positions.

sections.h2: How do I tell which ad version works?
paras: Wait several days, and do not call a winner from one afternoon or from a version that hardly played.

Read three numbers in order. First, how many people stay past the opening, which tells you if the start works. Second, the click rate, which tells you if people wanted to visit. Third, the cost per purchase or per add-to-cart, which matters most for the shop. A version can win on views and still lose on sales. If the numbers land close, that change did not matter much. Keep the one you prefer and test a bigger difference next.
sections.alt: Hands rest beside blank color cards and the same plain round wall clock.

sections.h2: What should the next test change?
paras: Turn off the clear losers, keep the version that brings sales at a cost you can live with, and change one new thing.

Write down the date, what changed, and the result. After a few rounds you will see what your buyers respond to. When a winner starts costing more per sale, make fresh versions. Work through opening, setting, shape, length, then the offer. Each round starts from what already worked.

faq.q: How many versions should a small shop run?
faq.a: Start with a few, often three. More than that splits a small budget so thin that no version gets a fair look, and every extra version is another job.
Test the opening. It decides whether anyone watches the rest. Keep the product, the length, and the shape the same until that result is clear.

faq.q: Can I change the price on only one version?
faq.a: Not if you are testing the picture. Put the same line, price, and music on every file. Test the offer in a later round, on its own.

faq.q: Where do the numbers come from?
faq.a: From your ad account, where real viewers produce the result. The versions are made here. The comparison happens there.

faq.q: What if one version gets almost no spend?
faq.a: Do not treat it as a loser. Use the account's built-in test, or separate groups, so each version actually runs.

faq.q: How many credits does a test round use?
